title: SECOND PROPERTY TAX PAYMENT DUE
full_story:
The second installment of the 2025 payable 2026 Real Estate Tax Bill is due in one week, on Friday, November 20th.  If you have questions about your tax bill, please feel free to call the Treasurer’s office.  If you cannot get through, please leave a message, and they will return your call as soon as possible.  Phone 618-665-3727.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.

At the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money order.  Bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday through Friday but closed on national holidays.

Online by credit/debit card: Go to www.govpaynow.com PLC #a00082.

Or by drop box at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

title: SATURDAY TAILGATE
full_story:
The Flora Wolves Football Team will host West Frankfort tomorrow at 3 pm in the quarterfinals of the Class 2A IHSA Football Tournament.

There will be a game day field goal contest at 12:30 and other contests for the kids.  The gates open at 1pm.  There will also be free face painting, corn hole, and music.

title: POOLE TO BE INDUCTED
full_story:
The National Athletic Hall of Fame Selection Committee will induct Randy Poole in the Media – Sports Broadcaster category tonight, at the Teutopolis Banquet Hall in Teutopolis.

For more than three decades, Randy was one of the most recognizable voices in regional athletics.  He served as the longtime broadcaster for Flora Wolves football (34 years) and Flora Wolves basketball (15 years) on WNOI, becoming a trusted and familiar presence for generations of athletes, families, and fans.  In addition to his play-by-play work, Poole also spent 15 years as Sports Director, covering football, basketball, baseball, softball, and junior high athletics throughout the region.

Randy’s dedication extends far beyond the broadcast booth.  He has been an active member of the Flora Rotary Club for 30 years, served on the Flora Academic Foundation Board and the Flora Chamber of Commerce, and remains a committed member of the First Methodist Church in Flora, where he serves on the Church Council.

The 2026 Induction Ceremony will again be held tonight starting at 6 pm at the Teutopolis Banquet Hall in Teutopolis.

title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Village of Noble Board of Trustees approved a 4% pay raise for village employees and addressed local storage container violations during its regular meeting.

Following a recommendation from the Personnel Committee, the board voted unanimously to grant a 4% wage increase for village workers.  Trustees also approved expanding the village’s use of Auto Pay for monthly bills, with a report to be provided showing payment dates and amounts.

In code enforcement matters, the board discussed unpermitted shipping containers at 253 East North Avenue and non-compliant containers at 128 West Poplar Street.  Officials noted the Poplar Street container violates local ordinances regarding paint and the removal of identifying markings.  The board directed the Building Official to speak with the residents about permit requirements and compliance.

Discussion on the Fiscal Year 26-27 tax levy was tabled until the next meeting.  Board members requested more details on the aggregate property tax percentage from village accountant Kapper before taking action.  Clerk Cindy Manuel will also research several questions regarding the Water Fund before scheduling a Water Committee meeting.

Mayor Kessler also announced several reminders Leaf Collection runs Monday through Thursday from 8:00 am to 3:00 pm.  Residents should call Village Hall to schedule a pickup.  The Noble Lions Club Pancake Breakfast: Scheduled for Saturday, from 7:00 to 11:00 am.  And the Noble Village Hall will be closed November 26th and 27th for Thanksgiving.

title: OPERATION CHRISTMAS CHILD
full_story:
Nearly 5,000 drop-off locations for Operation Christmas Child will open Monday.

According to a news release, volunteers across the country will be preparing to collect shoeboxes for this year’s Operation Christmas Child, one of the projects of Samaritan’s Purse.  Over the last 33 years, the project has collected and delivered shoeboxes filled with toys, school supplies, and personal care items to millions of children around the world.  Many of those children are suffering from war, poverty, disease and disaster.

For those who wish to participate in this year’s project, you can find a step-by-step guide on the How to Pack a Shoebox the link in this story Operation Christmas Child.  The project partners with different churches across the world to deliver the boxes once they’ve been collected. You can also donate $10 per shoebox gift online through “Follow Your Box” to receive a tracking label and discover its destination.

“Shoebox gifts may seem simple, but they have an eternal impact.  Each box is an opportunity to tell a boy or girl in need about the true meaning of Christmas,” said Franklin Graham, president of Samaritan’s Purse.  “I’ve delivered these boxes around the world, and I never get tired of seeing the joy that they bring, even in the midst of disasters, war, and poverty.”

Operation Christmas Child has collected and delivered more than 244 million gift-filled shoeboxes and delivered them to children in more than 175 countries and territories.

Collection week is set for November 16 through November 23rd.  In Flora the drop off location is Christ’s Church, packages will be collected Monday, from 1 to 3 pm and from 5 to 7 pm.  On Tuesday from 9 to 11 am, Wednesday, from 1 to 3 pm, Thursday, from 9 to 11am, Friday, November 20th from 1 to 3 pm and from 5 to 7 pm, on Saturday, November 21st from 10 to Noon, on Sunday, November 22nd from 9:30 am to 1:30 pm and on Monday, November 23rd from 7 to 9 am.

title: TURKEY HUNTERS RESULTS
full_story:
Turkey hunters in Illinois harvested a preliminary total of 257 wild turkeys during the 2026 fall firearm season, compared with 255 in 2025.  The nine-day season ran October 24th through November 1st.

In Clay County hunters harvested 8 turkeys this year compared to 5 last year.  Jefferson County’s harvest was also up this year, with hunters taking 17 compared to 16 last year.  Wayne County’s Turkey harvest remained steady at 11 and all other counties in our area had lowers harvest numbers.

A total of 1,911 regular fall firearm turkey permits were sold, compared to 1,763 in 2025.  An additional 20,154 landowner permits were issued in 2026, compared to 19,370 in 2025.

The top counties for harvest were Jo Daviess, 21; Jackson, 19; Jefferson, 17; Union, 15; and Williamson, 13.  Preliminary harvest reports identified 138 female birds (54%) and 116 male birds (46%).  The sex of three birds was unknown.

title: RETABULATION OF BLAIR PRECINCT
full_story:
The Clay County Clerk’s Office has announced it will conduct a post-election retabulation and official canvass for the November 3rd General Election.

County Clerk Amy Britton issued a memorandum stating that the Illinois State Board of Elections randomly selected the Blair precinct for retabulation.  The county is also required to test its early voting equipment, specifically the Freedom Vote Scan Tabulator number 43102, which handles all early voting precincts.

The retabulation process will take place at the County Clerk’s office on Monday, starting at 10:00 am.  Following the retabulation, election officials will count any valid, late-returned mail-in ballots and run the official election canvass, which is expected to begin at approximately 11:00 am.

title: GATEWAY CHANGES DISINFECTANT
full_story:
Beginning Monday Gateway Regional Water Company will begin a modified disinfection process using Free Chlorine instead of Chloramines for its predominant water disinfectant.  Beginning December 21st, they will switch back from Free Chlorine residual to the normal Chloramines residual for its predominant water disinfectant.

Customers with health issues should contact their physicians with any health-related questions.

Customers on Gateway Regional Water Company include the City of Flora; Clay County Water; Western Wayne Water Company; Village of Xenia; Village of Iuka; City of Kinmundy; Village of Alma; Village of Farina; Fayette Water Company; FMC Water Co.; NEMC Water Co.; Village of Patoka; Raccoon Water Co.; and Village of Vernon.

If you have any questions, please contact Gateway at 618-775-1004.

title: VETERANS ACT PASSED
full_story:
U.S. Representative Mike Bost, the chairman of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee, celebrated House passage of his landmark Take Care of America’s Veterans Act.  The legislation expands healthcare and mental health access, advances education and job opportunities, supports Gold Star families, and delivers the Major Richard Star Act to over 60,000 disabled veterans.

“The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act is a historic healthcare and benefits expansion that will positively impact millions of veterans and American families,” said Bost.  “This landmark bill reduces the wounded veteran tax, expands mental health options, improves the Transition Assistance Program, and ensures veterans and their families can access the healthcare and benefits they’ve earned.  For the first time in years, we have a pathway to deliver these historic reforms at VA, and I’m committed to working with the Senate to get this bill to the president’s desk before the end of the year.  This legislation will make a difference for Gold Star families, caregivers, and veterans living with the wounds of military service.  It will help families make ends meet and uphold the promise we made to those who served.  With the House passing this bill on Veterans Day, my message to our veteran community is simple: House Republicans – America – has got your back.”

“From the first American soldiers who defeated the most powerful army on Earth, to the liberators of Europe during World War II, to the heroes who answered the call of duty after our nation was attacked on 9/11, American veterans have played an indispensable role in the history and unmatched success of our republic.  For their sacrifice and service, we have a duty to uphold the promise this country made to the men and women who pledged their lives to defend it,” said Speaker Mike Johnson.  “The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act keeps that promise by strengthening health care and mental health services, expanding education and economic opportunities, modernizing veterans’ benefits, and supporting the caregivers and military families who serve alongside our veterans.  This legislation delivers for every veteran and every future man or woman who will answer the call to put on the uniform, and we are grateful to Chairman Bost and the Veterans’ Affairs Committee for their work to get this transformational package across the finish line.”
